blindSummary: Sodomy is criminalised in this country (1 year, both sexes — a domestic-origin law; the country was never colonised); a legislator is seeking support for a harsh 2024 anti-homosexuality bill (so far unsuccessful); mob violence is documented; there is no legal gender recognition.
blindOutOfScope: Active hostile bill (2024) not yet passed.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying legal-aid trust country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex activity (misdemeanour, up to 1 year).

Criminalisation-monitoring outlet (Oct 2024): a legislator in this country is seeking supporters for a harsh anti-homosexuality bill - raising penalties to 10 years (life for repeat/'aggravated' offences), imprisoning children as young as 10, and outlawing LGBTIQ+ advocacy and 'promotion of homosexuality'; so far he has announced no success attracting supporters.

Joint UN development-agency and human-rights-office country report (April 2020): participatory review and analysis of the legal, social and human-rights environment for people of diverse sexual orientation and gender identity in this country.

Foreign public-radio network (April 2012): LGBT rights here come under the spotlight - anti-gay sentiment has grown since a large foreign government announced plans to promote LGBT rights overseas; new legislation calls for longer jail terms for homosexuality; fliers target gay-rights supporters.

Foreign broadsheet (March 2012): this country's president defended its law criminalising homosexual acts - saying the country's people like themselves just the way they are - in a joint interview with a visibly uncomfortable former head of government of another large foreign country.

The country's 2015 decent work act (full text): the national labour law - fundamental rights at work, employment, institutions; relevant as the statutory framework within which workplace discrimination protections would sit.
blindTangential: Sodomy criminalised (1 year, both sexes) — formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the 2024 bill (not passed) signals trajectory.
